topic: why giant raindrops are physically impossible
title: The Physics Reason Giant Raindrops Are Impossible
description: Could a whole storm's worth of rain ever merge into one giant raindrop? Physics says no -- here's the actual size limit and why it exists, every time, in every storm. AI-narrated science commentary.

beats.text: A giant raindrop the size of a football field could never actually form -- no matter how big the storm.
Real raindrops top out around five millimeters across, roughly a pea, before gravity ever gets a bigger chance.
As a drop falls faster, air resistance flattens it out, more like a hamburger bun than a teardrop.
Push it past that size and surface tension can't hold on -- the drop shreds into smaller droplets mid-air.

beats.text: So even inside the fiercest thunderstorm, physics keeps hitting reset on raindrop size, over and over.
Meteorologists actually use that breakup limit to read storm intensity off radar in real time.
